origin.description: Raw, ratio, and regression estimates of quantiles of a bootstrap statistic under importance resampling.
origin.usage: imp.quantile(boot.out = NULL, alpha = NULL, index = 1, t = boot.out$t[, index], w = NULL, def = TRUE, q = NULL)

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A boot object from boot or tilt.boot. Required when t or the importance weights are not supplied.

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.text: Quantile levels. The default is 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.95, 0.975, and 0.99.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: Column of boot.out$t to use when t is not supplied. Only the first element is used.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates of the statistic. The default is the selected column of boot.out$t.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Importance weights, one per replicate. If omitted, they are computed by imp.weights.

arguments.name: def
arguments.text: Passed to imp.weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: Target resampling probabilities, passed to imp.weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

origin.details: Non-finite replicates are dropped, along with their weights. Replicates are ordered, and a quantile is the largest ordered value whose cumulative weight is at most (R+1)*alpha. The ratio cumulative weight divides by the mean weight. The regression cumulative weight uses the regression weights from imp.reg. For a raw level above one half, the cumulative weights are built by indexing the sorted weights with the reversed order permutation, and the selected value is negated. An empty selection is -Inf, so that upper raw tail can be Inf.
origin.value: A list with components alpha, raw, rat, and reg. raw, rat, and reg each have one quantile per level in alpha.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(boot))
set.seed(1)
x <- c(10, 12, 9, 15, 11, 14)
weights <- c(0.05, 0.15, 0.1, 0.3, 0.25, 0.15)
statistic <- function(d, w) sum(d * w) / sum(w)
b <- boot(x, statistic, R = 12, stype = "w", weights = weights)
print(imp.quantile(b, alpha = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)))

translation.usage: imp_quantile(boot_out=None, alpha=None, index=1, t=None, w=None, def_=True, q=None)

arguments.name: boot_out
arguments.text: Bootstrap object with t, t0, data, weights, strata, R, and frequency. Required when t or the importance weights are omitted. frequency is the resample count matrix copied from boot.array.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based column of t to use when t is omitted. Only the first element is used.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates of the statistic. Omitted means the selected column of boot_out.t.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Importance weights, one per replicate. Omitted means they are computed by imp_weights.

arguments.name: def_
arguments.text: This is def in R. Passed to imp_weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: Target resampling probabilities, passed to imp_weights when the weights are computed. Ignored when w is supplied.

translation.details: Non-finite replicates are dropped, along with their weights. Replicates are ordered, and a quantile is the largest ordered value whose cumulative weight is at most (R+1)*alpha. The ratio cumulative weight divides by the mean weight. The regression cumulative weight uses the regression weights. For a raw level above one half, the cumulative weights are built by indexing the sorted weights with the reversed order permutation, and the selected value is negated.
